response:
The work required to double the gap equals the change in stored energy. With the capacitor disconnected, charge remains constant. Initial energy: \( U_i = \frac{1}{2} C_i V_i^2 \) where \( C_i = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d} = 1.78 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{F} \). So \( U_i = 8.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{J} \). After doubling the gap, the energy doubles, so the work is \( U_i \). Thus the work is \( 8.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{J} \).  
The charge on the soap bubble is given by \( Q = 4\pi \varepsilon_0 R V \). With \( R = 0.01 \, \text{m} \), \( V = 100 \, \text{V} \), and \( \varepsilon_0 = 8.9 \times 10^{-12} \, \text{C}^2/(\text{N·m}^2) \), we compute \( Q = 4\pi (8.9\times 10^{-12})(0.01)(100) = 1.1 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{C} \) (rounded to two significant figures).

ANSWER: 8.9e-5,1.1e-10
